basis: Testicular malignancy is reproductive; endocrine dysfunction and hematologic subtypes are not defining across this umbrella.
Generalized atherosclerotic disease directly affects arteries; downstream organ infarctions are separate complications.
Site-unspecified extragonadal tumor umbrella, commonly mediastinal or retroperitoneal; no listed organ origin applies across most cases.
Hemoglobin disorder causing anemia and ineffective erythropoiesis; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage; fibrosis and skeletal disease are occasional.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive skin inflammation and sterile pyogenic arthritis.
Lysosomal storage neurodegeneration; progressive retinal degeneration with visual loss occurs commonly (>30%) in late-infantile CLN8 disease.
Bony bridging of the sella turcica is a skeletal anomaly; pituitary dysfunction is not established.
Congenital absence of nasal structures/airways; microphthalmia or eyelid coloboma and microtia each occur at 30-79%; olfactory defects lack frequency evidence.
Hereditary motor neuropathy; vocal cord paresis/paralysis is a defining type 7 manifestation causing laryngeal dysfunction.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; strabismus affects 3/8 (38%).
Familial early-onset Alzheimer neurodegeneration affects the brain.
Disorder of neurologic circadian sleep-wake regulation; no additional organ damage is established.
Epilepsy, intellectual deterioration and dental enamel defects define the syndrome; impaired sweating occurs in 30-79%.
Respiratory-system malformation umbrella; additional skeletal involvement depends on the specific thoracic subtype.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood cells and marrow; trisomy 8 does not establish another affected organ.
HSV infection directly inflames and ulcerates the oral mucosa and gums.
The defining phenotype combines metaphyseal bone abnormalities, skin lesions and spastic paraplegia.
Naegleria fowleri directly infects and destroys brain and meningeal tissue.
Thrombosis of cerebral veins and venous sinuses defines this cerebrovascular disorder; associated infections are separate conditions.
Visual impairment 8/12; muscle pathology 3/5 and contractures 5/12. Ventilatory failure 5/12 does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Hepatitis A virus causes acute inflammatory liver injury; arthralgia does not establish joint damage.
Pituitary ischemic necrosis causes hormone deficiencies; progressive visual field defects are annotated as frequent (30-79%).
Skeletal anomalies and steroidogenesis defects define disease; choanal stenosis 1/3. Hypertension 1/3 is sparse evidence; single umbilical artery is fetal anatomy.
Congenital muscle-brain-eye dystroglycanopathy; myopia occurs in 30-79%, with other structural eye anomalies variably present; cardiomyopathy is occasional.
Benign fibro-osseous neoplasm originating in bone; adjacent sinus or orbital extension is site-dependent.
